QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_13

question.text: In the mutual fund trust structure in India, the Trustees - acting as guardians of unitholder interests - appoint which entity to manage the day-to-day investment of the fund's assets?

explanation.text: The Logic: In India's mutual fund trust structure, the Sponsor establishes the trust; the Trustees are then appointed to safeguard unitholder interests. The Trustees in turn appoint the Asset Management Company (AMC) to manage the fund's day-to-day investments. The framing here matches the page-99 overview where Trustees appoint the AMC to manage the fund. The Trap: SEBI is the regulator, not an appointor in the trust structure; the Custodian holds the securities but does not manage investments; Unitholders do not directly appoint the AMC. The audit flagged the original because the option list contained "Sponsor" alongside "Trustees" - and page 100 of the Series II-B workbook does allow AMCs to be appointed by the Sponsor or Trustees if authorized by the trust deed, so the original was defensible for either answer. Note: The original was ambiguous because of the Sponsor-vs-Trustees tension between pages 99 and 100 of the NISM Series II-B (December 2025) workbook. The stem has been constrained to the page-99 overview (Trustees appoint the AMC) and the Sponsor distractor has been replaced by "Custodian", leaving "Asset Management Company (AMC)" as the uniquely correct answer the Trustees appoint.
